# QA — doodle-jump_gemini-cli.html

**Artifact:** `games/doodle-jump_gemini-cli.html` (923 LOC, single file)
**Generated by:** Gemini CLI
**Audit date:** 2026-06-04
**Method:** static code review (no runtime testing)

## Summary

The leanest of the three variants. Solid core gameplay loop with proper delta-frame collision (prevBottom check), spring/rocket/propeller items, monsters, black holes, and a 5-entry leaderboard in `localStorage`. Several real bugs in the pause/resume flow and resilience (corrupt-storage, mid-game resize, multi-touch). Visually plain but functionally complete.

---

## Critical

_(none — game is fully playable, no crash on golden path)_

---

## Major

### M1 — Double `requestAnimationFrame` loop after resume
**Location:** `gameLoop()` lines 880–897, `togglePause()` lines 669–679
While paused, `gameLoop()` still recurses every frame (the early-return inside the function only skips `update/draw`; the rAF call at line 895 fires regardless because `gameState === 'playing'`). When `togglePause()` flips `isPaused` back to false, it **also** calls `gameLoop()` again at line 674 — now two rAF chains run in parallel for the rest of the session: double physics step, double score increments, and the game runs at ~2× speed.
**Fix:** either cancel the in-flight `animationId` before calling `gameLoop()` in `togglePause`, or stop scheduling new frames while `isPaused === true`.

### M2 — Mid-game `resize` leaves player/platforms outside new viewport
**Location:** `resizeCanvas()` line 169
On window resize the canvas dimensions are updated but `player.x`, platform `x`, and `nextSpawnY` are not rescaled. On a portrait→landscape rotation or browser-window resize, the player and existing platforms can end up off-screen, the camera offset is now wrong relative to the new height, and the spawn band misalignments may leave the player stuck mid-air with no platforms beneath.
**Fix:** during a live game, scale all world coordinates by the W/H ratio change, or freeze the game until the next round.

### M3 — Multi-touch breaks input
**Location:** `touchstart` line 231, `touchend` line 242
`touchstart` looks at `e.touches[0]` only, and `touchend` unconditionally clears **both** `touchLeft` and `touchRight`. Holding the right side, tapping the left, then releasing the left releases the right too — player drifts. Multi-finger play (one finger left, one right, alternating) doesn't work.
**Fix:** key the touch state by `touch.identifier`; only clear the side whose finger lifted.

### M4 — Corrupt `localStorage` crashes the game on load
**Location:** line 200, `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('doodle_leaderboard'))`
No `try/catch`. If `doodle_leaderboard` exists but is malformed (interrupted write, manual edit, foreign data), the script throws on load and the page never renders the menu. There's no recovery path; the user has to clear storage manually.
**Fix:** wrap in `try/catch` and fall back to `[0,0,0,0,0]`.

### M5 — Game keeps requesting animation frames after game-over for "particle fade" indefinitely
**Location:** `gameLoop()` line 886
`gameState === 'gameover' && particles.length > 0` keeps the loop alive — fine, but combined with M1 (double-loop) the post-game-over particle update can also run twice. Single-loop is correct.

---

## Medium

### m1 — Missing `roundRect` fallback for older Safari
**Location:** lines 418, 523
`CanvasRenderingContext2D.roundRect` requires Safari 16+ / Chrome 99+. On older browsers the entire render loop throws.
**Fix:** add a small polyfill or use `arcTo` paths.

### m2 — Leaderboard initialized with `[0,0,0,0,0]` shows "1. 0  2. 0 …" on first launch
**Location:** lines 138, 200
A first-time player sees a populated leaderboard of zeros — confusing and visually noisy.
**Fix:** initialize as `[]` and render "No scores yet" until populated.

### m3 — Score is measured in pixels, not rounded to a meaningful unit
**Location:** line 749, `Math.floor(Math.abs(cameraY))`
Score climbs by ~10/frame and reaches 5-digit values within seconds. No design issue per se, but harder to recognize meaningful milestones than the other variants' score-per-platform model.

### m4 — `isColliding` uses simple AABB but platform collision relies on `vy > 0` + position guard, while item/enemy use plain AABB
**Location:** lines 770, 787
Items/enemies are detected with full overlap — if the player passes through an enemy from below while jumping fast, they collide for one frame and die regardless of vertical position relative to the enemy's hitbox. Players can lose runs to a top-of-jump grazing collision.
**Fix:** distinguish "stomp" (vy>0, above center) from "die" (any other overlap) the same way enemies of type 0 do — currently only monsters allow stomping.

### m5 — `gameOver` doesn't clean up `enemies`, `items`, `particles` arrays before re-using on retry
**Location:** lines 696–700
On retry, `startGame` reassigns each array to `[]` so it works. But `animationId` is not always canceled before the new loop starts; combined with M1 it can compound. (Same root as M1.)

### m6 — No "new record" indicator
After 5 scores are saved, the new score is just inserted into the sorted top-5 silently. Less rewarding feedback than the other two variants.

---

## Minor

- **n1** — `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` meta is missing; the other two variants set it. iOS home-screen launch shows a Safari chrome.
- **n2** — `Audio.gain` and friends recreate an oscillator per beep without explicit cleanup — Web Audio garbage-collects oscillators on `stop`, so it's fine, but each call leaks a tiny graph for one frame.
- **n3** — Comments are minimal/absent. Given the audience (comparison playground) this is fine, but a reader has to infer that `type` indices on Platform mean `0=normal, 1=moving, 2=breakable, 3=spring, 4=disappearing` (only present in inline comments, not extracted to a const).
- **n4** — `pauseBtnUI` uses literal `II` text instead of the unicode pause symbol `⏸` (the Claude variant uses the proper symbol).
- **n5** — Pause button on touch devices: `touchstart` on `gameContainer` has `e.preventDefault()` after a `pauseBtnUI` early return — works, but mixing the pause button's own click handler with a parent touch listener is fragile.

---

## What's good

- Cleanest, smallest implementation of the three — easy to read top-to-bottom.
- Correct **prevBottom** check for platform collision (`prevPlayerBottom <= p.y + 10 && playerBottom >= p.y`) — only lands on a platform from above.
- Web Audio synthesis with five distinct sound effects.
- Difficulty ramp via `Math.min(score / 10000, 1)` modulates platform-type weights.
- Particle system used for game-over death animation.
